description: A small, colorful sunfish common in lakes and ponds.
fun_fact: Can make grunting sounds by grinding their teeth together.
name: Bluegill

description: A hardy, bottom-feeding fish found in almost every waterway.
fun_fact: Can live over 40 years and remember the locations of food sources.
name: Common Carp

description: A popular panfish with distinctive vertical stripes.
fun_fact: Their eggs are laid in long accordion-like ribbons that can stretch over two metres.
name: Yellow Perch

description: A brilliantly coloured sunfish with orange and blue markings.
fun_fact: One of the few freshwater fish that can crush and eat snails whole.
name: Pumpkinseed

description: A whiskered bottom-dweller with a keen sense of taste.
fun_fact: Has taste buds distributed across its entire body, including its skin and barbels.
name: Channel Catfish

description: A schooling panfish prized for its mild, flaky meat.
fun_fact: Its name comes from the Canadian French word crapet, used for various sunfish species.
name: Crappie

description: A spirited fish born in freshwater that can adapt to the sea.
fun_fact: When rainbow trout migrate to the ocean and return, they are called steelhead, technically the same species.
name: Rainbow Trout

description: An aggressive predator and one of the most sought sport fish.
fun_fact: Can see colour and uses it to identify and target specific prey.
name: Largemouth Bass

description: A feisty fighter that punches well above its weight class.
fun_fact: Strongly territorial and will aggressively rearrange rocks and debris to protect their nests.
name: Smallmouth Bass

description: A cunning, selective trout known for frustrating anglers.
fun_fact: Has been introduced to every continent except Antarctica, making it one of the most widely spread freshwater fish on Earth.
name: Brown Trout

description: An apex freshwater predator with a mouthful of razor teeth.
fun_fact: Can swallow prey up to half its own body size in a single strike.
name: Northern Pike

description: The largest pike family member, rare, powerful, and legendary.
fun_fact: Nicknamed "the fish of ten thousand casts" by anglers who spend seasons pursuing a single specimen.
name: Muskellunge

description: A fast, schooling fish with striking iridescent markings.
fun_fact: Cannot stop swimming or they will suffocate, since they breathe only by moving forward through the water.
name: Atlantic Mackerel

description: One of the most abundant fish in the ocean, found in vast schools.
fun_fact: Communicate with each other at night using flatulence, releasing and detecting high-frequency sounds from expelled gas bubbles.
name: Atlantic Herring

description: A warm-blooded tuna that travels in massive mixed-species schools.
fun_fact: Like mammals, they can regulate their own body temperature, keeping muscles warm for explosive speed.
name: Skipjack Tuna

description: A streamlined, striped cousin of the tuna built for speed.
fun_fact: Its dried, fermented form, katsuobushi, is one of the most fundamental ingredients in Japanese dashi broth.
name: Bonito

description: A ferocious pack hunter known for its slashing, violent strikes.
fun_fact: Will enter a feeding frenzy and continue attacking fish even when completely full, leaving trails of destruction.
name: Bluefish

description: A powerful migratory fish that moves between salt and fresh water.
fun_fact: Migrates hundreds of miles up rivers to spawn each spring, returning to the same rivers year after year.
name: Striped Bass

description: A remarkable fish capable of gliding long distances through the air.
fun_fact: Can glide over 400 metres on a single launch, using ocean updrafts to stay airborne.
name: Flying Fish

description: A deep-bodied, fast-running fish prized for its exceptional flavour.
fun_fact: Widely considered one of the finest eating fish in the world by professional chefs.
name: Pompano

description: A powerful, solitary predator often found shadowing larger animals.
fun_fact: Regularly follows sharks, rays, and even sea turtles, eating scraps and prey flushed out by their movements.
name: Cobia

description: One of the fastest fish in the ocean, a torpedo with teeth.
fun_fact: Capable of burst speeds up to 60 mph, making it one of the fastest fish ever recorded.
name: Wahoo

description: A hard-fighting deepwater predator known for powerful runs.
fun_fact: Known to deliberately ram fishing lines with their head in an attempt to break free.
name: Amberjack

description: A sleek, toothy predator with razor-sharp eyesight.
fun_fact: Have excellent vision and are strongly attracted to shiny objects, which they mistake for the flash of fleeing prey.
name: Barracuda

description: A brilliantly coloured open-ocean fish of striking beauty.
fun_fact: One of the fastest-growing fish in the ocean, reaching full adult size in as little as one year.
name: Mahi-mahi

description: A fast, toothy migratory fish that runs in large schools.
fun_fact: Females far outlive males and can reach 26 years old, decades longer than most males in the same population.
name: King Mackerel

description: A cornerstone of Atlantic fisheries for centuries.
fun_fact: Once so abundant off North America that colonists reportedly walked across their backs, now critically threatened.
name: Atlantic Cod

description: A cod relative identified by its distinctive dark shoulder mark.
fun_fact: The dark mark behind the pectoral fin is called the "Devil's thumbprint," from a legend that the Devil squeezed it when Christ performed the miracle of the loaves and fishes.
name: Haddock

description: A prized table fish and cunning predator of rocky reefs.
fun_fact: Highly territorial, with individuals observed rearranging shells and rocks to mark and decorate their home turf.
name: Sea Bass

description: A deep reef dweller with vivid colouring and firm white flesh.
fun_fact: Can live over 50 years, and scientists age them by counting rings on tiny ear bones, just like trees.
name: Red Snapper

description: A powerful, serpentine predator lurking in reef crevices.
fun_fact: Has a second set of jaws hidden in its throat that shoot forward to grip and pull prey inward, just like the creature in the Alien films.
name: Moray Eel

description: A ferocious ambush predator of the Pacific coast.
fun_fact: Not actually a cod, and its raw flesh runs naturally blue-green from a pigment called biliverdin.
name: Lingcod

description: A massive, slow-moving predator that ambushes prey whole.
fun_fact: All grouper start life female, and the largest and most dominant eventually changes sex and becomes male.
name: Grouper

description: The largest of all flatfish, capable of reaching enormous size.
fun_fact: Born swimming upright with eyes on both sides of its head, then one eye migrates over to join the other.
name: Halibut

description: A slender, wide-ranging shark found in oceans worldwide.
fun_fact: Travel in single-sex schools and may migrate over 5,000 miles in a single season, crossing entire ocean basins.
name: Blue Shark

description: A spectacular fish famous for its enormous sail-like dorsal fin.
fun_fact: Raises its sail to herd schools of fish into tight bait balls, then slashes through them at high speed.
name: Atlantic Sailfish

description: One of the largest and most powerful sport fish in the ocean.
fun_fact: The bill is not used to spear prey; it slashes sideways through schools of fish at speed, stunning them.
name: Blue Marlin

description: The fastest shark in the ocean and a spectacular fighter.
fun_fact: Capable of leaping over 20 feet clear of the water and sustaining speeds no other shark can match.
name: Mako Shark

description: A solitary, powerful predator of the open deep ocean.
fun_fact: Has a unique heat organ around its eyes and brain that warms them for sharper vision in cold, dark water.
name: Swordfish

description: A deep-sea predator that lures prey with a bioluminescent fishing rod.
fun_fact: The glowing lure is produced by colonies of bioluminescent bacteria living inside it; the fish provides shelter, the bacteria provide light.
name: Anglerfish

description: A bizarre deep-sea eel with an enormous hinged jaw.
fun_fact: Its mouth can open wide enough to swallow prey larger than its own body, and its stomach stretches to match.
name: Gulper Eel

description: A small but ferocious deep-sea predator covered in light organs.
fun_fact: Produces red bioluminescence, a wavelength most deep-sea creatures cannot see, giving it an invisible spotlight to hunt with.
name: Dragonfish

description: A fearsome-looking deep-sea fish with disproportionately huge teeth.
fun_fact: Has the largest teeth relative to body size of any fish in the ocean.
name: Fangtooth

description: A deep-sea ambush predator with fang-like teeth and a lure.
fun_fact: Uses bioluminescent light organs along its belly to camouflage itself against faint surface light, hiding from predators below.
name: Viperfish

description: A living fossil with an eel-like body and 300 trident-shaped teeth.
fun_fact: Looks almost unchanged from sharks that prowled the oceans 80 million years ago, and is rarely seen alive.
name: Frilled Shark

description: A strange fish with a transparent fluid-filled dome for a head.
fun_fact: Its actual eyes are green cylinders inside its transparent dome, and they rotate to look upward.
name: Barreleye

description: The internet's favourite fish, but looks very different in its home.
fun_fact: Only looks blobby at the surface; pressure changes on the way up cause it to decompress and deflate.
name: Blobfish

description: The world's longest bony fish, almost never seen alive.
fun_fact: Reaches up to 11 metres in length and is almost certainly the origin of ancient sea serpent legends around the world.
name: Oarfish

description: A prehistoric fish once thought extinct for 65 million years.
fun_fact: Was known only from fossils until a live specimen was caught off South Africa in 1938, shocking the scientific world.
name: Coelacanth

description: A small bioluminescent fish that forms vast schools in the mesopelagic zone.
fun_fact: Lanternfish may account for up to 65% of all deep-sea fish biomass, making them one of the most abundant vertebrates on Earth.
name: Lanternfish

description: A silvery, flat-bodied fish with large upward-pointing eyes adapted for dim deep water.
fun_fact: Hatchetfish produce bioluminescent light from their bellies to match faint light from above, making them nearly invisible to predators below.
name: Hatchetfish

description: A tiny, nearly transparent fish found in staggering numbers throughout the deep ocean.
fun_fact: Bristlemouths may be the most abundant vertebrate on the entire planet, with billions inhabiting the world's deep waters.
name: Bristlemouth

description: A large-headed, tapering fish common on the abyssal plain, also called a rattail.
fun_fact: Grenadiers have been found below 6,000 metres and are among the most widespread fish families in the deep sea.
name: Grenadier

description: Neither a true squid nor an octopus, an ancient cephalopod that thrives in the oxygen-minimum zone.
fun_fact: Its name literally means "vampire squid from hell," yet it feeds only on marine snow and drifting detritus.
name: Vampire Squid

description: A small squid blanketed in photophores that pulse with vivid blue bioluminescent light.
fun_fact: Firefly squid have three types of photoreceptors, one of which may let them perceive colour, a rare ability among cephalopods.
name: Firefly Squid

description: Named for the large ear-like fins it flaps to glide through the deepest ocean floors.
fun_fact: Dumbo octopuses live deeper than any other known octopus, with some recorded below 7,000 metres.
name: Dumbo Octopus

description: A small fish with an enormous expandable stomach capable of engulfing prey far larger than itself.
fun_fact: Black swallowers have been found dead at the surface after prey they swallowed decomposed faster than they could digest it, and the expanding gases floated them up.
name: Black Swallower

description: A massive, armour-scaled predator that has prowled shallow rivers and coastal marshes largely unchanged for over 100 million years.
fun_fact: At 10 feet and 350 lbs, it's easy to see why early settlers thought it ate people.
name: Alligator Gar

description: The apex of open-ocean predators, a warm-blooded, torpedo-shaped giant that can cross the Atlantic in weeks.
fun_fact: A single Atlantic bluefin tuna sold for $3.1 million at Tokyo's Toyosu auction in 2019, making it the most valuable fish ever sold.
name: Atlantic Bluefin Tuna

description: One of the rarest sharks on Earth, a slow-moving, filter-feeding giant of the deep with a cavernous luminescent mouth.
fun_fact: Only discovered in 1976 when one tangled in a U.S. Navy anchor; fewer than 100 have ever been recorded.
name: Megamouth Shark

description: A massive, silver-scaled fish known for explosive leaps when hooked.
fun_fact: Tarpon can breathe air directly by gulping it at the surface, an ancient adaptation that lets them survive in oxygen-poor shallows.
name: Tarpon

description: The largest of the trevally family, a powerful, hard-fighting predator of coastal shallows.
fun_fact: Giant trevally have been documented leaping from the water to snatch seabirds in mid-flight.
name: Giant Trevally

description: One of the largest freshwater fish in the world, armoured in thick interlocking scales.
fun_fact: Arapaima scales can deflect piranha bites, and researchers study their structure to design better body armour.
name: Arapaima

description: One of the fastest fish in the sea, built like a torpedo with razor-sharp teeth.
fun_fact: Wahoo can accelerate past 75 km/h in short bursts, fast enough to strip a reel before you can react.
name: Roosterfish

description: A large, powerful pelagic fish prized for both its speed and its flavour.
fun_fact: Yellowfin tuna keep their body temperature several degrees above the surrounding water, giving their muscles extra power in cold open seas.
name: Yellowfin Tuna

description: A spectacular billfish known for high-speed runs and acrobatic leaps after being hooked.
fun_fact: Striped marlin herd baitfish into tight balls near the surface, then slash through them at speed with their bill.
name: Striped Marlin

description: A colossal cephalopod of the deep ocean, rarely encountered and never fully understood.
fun_fact: Giant squid have the largest eyes of any living animal, up to 30 cm across, to detect the faint bioluminescent glow of predators in the dark.
name: Giant Squid

fun_fact: Needlefish can leap from water at speeds up to 37 mph and have accidentally impaled fishermen with their needle-like beaks, making them unexpectedly dangerous for such a small fish.
name: Needlefish

fun_fact: Black Drum use chin barbels to feel for crabs and mollusks on the seafloor, and their powerful molar-like teeth to crush right through shells.
name: Black Drum

fun_fact: Blue Catfish can live over 20 years and grow to 150 pounds, the largest catfish in North America, getting bigger and more powerful every single year.
name: Blue Catfish

fun_fact: Brook Trout are actually char, not true trout, and are so sensitive to pollution they serve as a benchmark; if they're thriving, the water is genuinely clean.
name: Brook Trout

fun_fact: Flathead Catfish are solitary ambush predators that prefer live prey, lying motionless on riverbeds for hours waiting for a fish to swim within striking range.
name: Flathead Catfish

fun_fact: Grass Carp can eat three times their body weight in aquatic plants daily; introduced to control weeds, they sometimes consume everything and collapse entire ecosystems.
name: Grass Carp

fun_fact: Mudskippers breathe through their skin on land, climb mangrove roots using fins like crutches, and can survive out of water for days, making them one of the most amphibious fish alive.
name: Mudskipper

fun_fact: Pickerel are ambush predators that accelerate from dead still to full strike speed in under a second, faster than the human eye can follow.
name: Pickerel

fun_fact: Male Pink Salmon develop a large hump on their back during spawning season, earning them the nickname "humpies" and making them one of the most visually distinctive fish in the river.
name: Pink Salmon

fun_fact: Sheepshead have rows of flat, human-like teeth specifically designed to crush oysters, clams, and barnacles from rocks and dock pilings.
name: Sheepshead

fun_fact: Spotted Seatrout produce a drumming sound during spawning by rapidly contracting muscles against their swim bladder, audible to divers over a mile away.
name: Spotted Seatrout

fun_fact: Stingrays can detect electrical fields generated by prey buried in the sand, and their flat crushing teeth are perfectly designed for mollusks and crustaceans.
name: Stingray

fun_fact: Walleye have a reflective layer in their eyes that gives them exceptional night vision and makes their eyes glow eerily white when a light hits them in the dark.
name: Walleye

fun_fact: Atlantic Salmon can jump up to 10 feet to clear waterfalls during migration, and navigate back to the exact stream where they were born using Earth's magnetic field.
name: Atlantic Salmon

fun_fact: All Barramundi are born male and transition to female as they age, so a fish spawning as a male one year may be releasing eggs the next.
name: Barramundi

fun_fact: Bonefish can accelerate to 30 mph in inches of water and are so prized by fly fishermen they're almost universally released, earning the nickname "ghost of the flats."
name: Bonefish

fun_fact: Chinook Salmon are the largest Pacific salmon, sometimes exceeding 100 pounds, and travel up to 900 miles upstream to spawn in the exact gravel bed where they were born.
name: Chinook Salmon

fun_fact: Coho Salmon are the acrobats of Pacific salmon; when hooked, they leap and somersault repeatedly, sometimes launching six feet out of the water.
name: Coho Salmon

fun_fact: Electric Eels generate shocks of up to 860 volts, enough to stun a horse, and use weaker pulses to navigate and locate prey in complete darkness.
name: Electric Eel

fun_fact: No European Eel has ever been observed spawning; they travel 4,000 miles to the Sargasso Sea to reproduce and die, a journey that remains one of nature's greatest unsolved mysteries.
name: European Eel

fun_fact: Lake Trout are the largest freshwater char in North America and can live over 60 years, with the oldest confirmed individual at 62, older than most of the fishermen who pursue them.
name: Lake Trout

fun_fact: Seahorses are the only fish where the male becomes pregnant and gives birth; a single male can deliver up to 2,000 fry, and mated pairs hold tails while sleeping.
name: Seahorse

fun_fact: Snook are extremely temperature-sensitive, and cold snaps below 50°F can kill thousands at once, making them one of the most weather-dependent targets in saltwater fishing.
name: Snook

fun_fact: Sockeye Salmon turn brilliant crimson during spawning, and their flesh is the deepest orange-red of any salmon, a result of years feeding on krill and shrimp in the open ocean.
name: Sockeye Salmon

fun_fact: Steelhead Trout are the ocean-going form of Rainbow Trout, the same species, but those that migrate to sea grow twice as large and fight twice as hard.
name: Steelhead Trout

fun_fact: Archerfish shoot jets of water up to 10 feet with sniper accuracy, automatically accounting for light refraction at the surface, a physics calculation that takes human children years to master.
name: Archerfish

fun_fact: Sturgeon are living fossils that have survived five mass extinctions unchanged over 200 million years; some individuals live over 150 years, and females don't begin spawning until age 20.
name: Sturgeon

description: A small silver schooling fish found across the Atlantic and Mediterranean.
fun_fact: Despite their tiny size, anchovies are the second most-caught fish on Earth.
name: European Anchovy

description: Tiny but abundant, these silver fish travel in vast open-water schools.
fun_fact: A single sardine school can contain millions of fish, moving as one fluid mass.
name: Pacific Sardine

description: A common cold-water fish and staple of commercial fisheries worldwide.
fun_fact: Most imitation crab meat is made from pollock, the world's most processed fish.
name: Pollock

description: A vibrant royal-blue reef fish known for its sharp tail spine.
fun_fact: Blue tangs carry a hidden spine near the tail that locks in place as a defensive weapon.
name: Blue Tang

description: A bold orange-and-white fish that shelters among sea anemones.
fun_fact: All clownfish are born male; the dominant fish in a group will change sex to become female.
name: Clownfish

description: A flat ambush predator with both eyes on one side of its body.
fun_fact: Flounder hatch with eyes on both sides of their head, and one eye migrates as they grow.
name: Flounder

description: A large, bottom-hugging predator and one of the most-fished species on Earth.
fun_fact: Pacific cod can live up to 18 years and grow over a metre long in cold northern waters.
name: Pacific Cod

description: When threatened, this spiny fish inflates itself into an almost perfect sphere.
fun_fact: Pufferfish organs contain tetrodotoxin, one of the most potent natural poisons known.
name: Pufferfish

description: A fast, streamlined hunter with striking spots along its silver flanks.
fun_fact: Spanish mackerel are voracious hunters that slash through baitfish schools at high speed.
name: Spanish Mackerel

description: Named for the locking spine it uses to wedge itself into reef crevices.
fun_fact: Triggerfish are notorious for aggressively defending their nests and will charge snorkellers.
name: Triggerfish

description: An ambush predator that drifts motionless before snapping up prey with its long snout.
fun_fact: Trumpetfish sometimes hide directly behind larger fish, using them as cover to stalk prey.
name: Trumpetfish

description: A diamond-shaped flatfish prized for its firm, delicate white flesh.
fun_fact: Turbot can shift the colour and texture of their skin to vanish against the sandy seabed.
name: Turbot

description: A long-finned tuna that migrates thousands of miles across open ocean.
fun_fact: Albacore are the only tuna species whose flesh can legally be labelled as 'white tuna'.
name: Albacore Tuna

description: An agile reef shark recognized by the black tips on its fins.
fun_fact: Blacktip sharks are known to leap out of the water and spin up to three times before landing.
name: Blacktip Shark

description: A powerful, hard-fighting fish that inhabits offshore reefs and wrecks.
fun_fact: Greater amberjack are apex predators on deep reefs and can grow to over 60 kg.
name: Greater Amberjack

description: A muscular schooling predator notorious for its dogged, relentless fight.
fun_fact: Jack crevalle tolerate a wide salinity range and are often found in freshwater rivers.
name: Jack Crevalle

description: A beautiful but venomous reef fish whose spines pack a painful sting.
fun_fact: Lionfish are an invasive species in the Atlantic, where they have no natural predators.
name: Lionfish

description: A large reef grouper capable of changing color and sex throughout its life.
fun_fact: Nassau grouper gather in massive spawning aggregations of thousands at specific full moons.
name: Nassau Grouper

description: One of the largest flatfish in the world, haunting cold Pacific depths.
fun_fact: Pacific halibut can live over 55 years and reach weights exceeding 200 kg.
name: Pacific Halibut

description: A deep-bodied silver fish and one of the most prized catches in flats fishing.
fun_fact: The permit is considered one of the most difficult fish in the world to catch on a fly rod.
name: Permit

description: Known for the single dark spot near its tail, this drum fights hard in shallow bays.
fun_fact: The spot near the red drum's tail is thought to confuse predators into striking the wrong end.
name: Red Drum

description: A graceful ray adorned with white spots that leaps clear of the water.
fun_fact: Spotted eagle rays can launch themselves completely airborne, sometimes landing in boats.
name: Spotted Eagle Ray

description: The largest grouper in the Atlantic, capable of swallowing prey whole with a thunderous gulp.
fun_fact: Goliath grouper produce a booming percussive sound loud enough to stun prey and deter divers.
name: Goliath Grouper

description: A gentle giant of the open ocean that filters plankton through its wide, wing-like pectoral fins.
fun_fact: Manta rays have the largest brain-to-body ratio of any fish and can recognise themselves in mirrors.
name: Manta Ray

description: The fastest fish in the sea, capable of bursts exceeding 110 km/h with its iconic dorsal sail raised.
fun_fact: Sailfish hunt cooperatively, raising their sails to herd and disorient schools of smaller fish.
name: Sailfish

description: The largest fish alive, yet it feeds only on the tiniest plankton and small fish.
fun_fact: Despite being the size of a school bus, whale sharks are entirely harmless to humans.
name: Whale Shark

description: A prized billfish of the Atlantic that dazzles anglers with spectacular aerial acrobatics.
fun_fact: White marlin are one of the most acrobatic billfish, leaping repeatedly when hooked.
name: White Marlin

description: The largest flatfish in the Atlantic, growing to enormous sizes in cold northern waters.
fun_fact: Atlantic halibut are the world's largest flatfish, with some exceeding 300 kg and living over 50 years.
name: Atlantic Halibut

description: A deep-diving tuna that regulates its body temperature to hunt in the cold depths.
fun_fact: Bigeye tuna have unusually large eyes adapted to detect prey in the near-darkness of deep water.
name: Bigeye Tuna

description: One of the most aggressive sharks, equally comfortable in salt and freshwater.
fun_fact: Bull sharks have been found over 4,000 km up the Amazon River, far from the open ocean.
name: Bull Shark

description: Its wide, flattened head gives it a 360-degree field of vision to hunt rays and fish.
fun_fact: The hammerhead's broad head is packed with electroreceptors, letting it detect buried stingrays.
name: Hammerhead Shark

description: The world's heaviest bony fish, drifting through warm waters to sunbathe at the surface.
fun_fact: Ocean sunfish produce up to 300 million eggs at once, more than any other vertebrate on Earth.
name: Ocean Sunfish

description: Named for its striped markings, this apex predator eats nearly anything it encounters.
fun_fact: Tiger shark stomachs have contained licence plates, tyres, and even an entire chicken coop.
name: Tiger Shark

description: The ocean's most iconic apex predator, known for its extraordinary size and senses.
fun_fact: Great whites can detect a single drop of blood diluted across 100 litres of water from kilometres away.
name: Great White Shark

fun_fact: The only freshwater fish known to attack humans unprovoked, with 32 interlocking teeth that shear through flesh.
name: Goliath Tigerfish

fun_fact: Clocked at over 80 mph, it is believed to be the fastest fish in the ocean, quicker than a cheetah at full sprint.
name: Black Marlin

fun_fact: Carbon dating of their eye lenses has confirmed some Greenland sharks live over 500 years, the longest-lived vertebrates on Earth.
name: Greenland Shark

fun_fact: Its enormous hinged jaw can open wide enough to swallow prey larger than its own body, a useful adaptation when food is scarce.
name: Pelican Eel

fun_fact: Takes perfectly circular plugs of flesh from animals far larger than itself, including dolphins, whales, and even nuclear submarines.
name: Cookiecutter Shark

fun_fact: One of the only creatures on Earth that can produce and see red light, giving it a completely invisible headlamp to hunt in the dark.
name: Stoplight Loosejaw

description: An extinct giant shark, the largest predatory fish that ever lived.
fun_fact: Megalodon teeth are still found on ocean floors today, some as big as a human hand.
name: Megalodon

description: An extinct long-necked marine reptile from the Jurassic.
fun_fact: Despite the myths, plesiosaurs likely could not raise their necks swan-like out of water.
name: Plesiosaurus

description: An extinct armored fish from the Devonian period.
fun_fact: Its bite was among the most powerful of any fish, estimated at 8,000 pounds of force.
name: Dunkleosteus

description: An extinct giant marine lizard from the late Cretaceous.
fun_fact: Mosasaurs had two sets of teeth, one on the jaw and one on the roof of the mouth.
name: Mosasaurus

description: An extinct early whale with a long, snake-like body.
fun_fact: Its name means "king lizard," and it was misidentified as a reptile for decades before scientists confirmed it was an ancestor of modern whales.
name: Basilosaurus

description: An extinct giant ichthyosaur, one of the largest marine reptiles ever.
fun_fact: It had no teeth, and likely used suction to slurp up squid and soft-bodied prey whole.
name: Shastasaurus

description: A spiral-shelled cephalopod and one of the ocean's oldest living lineages.
fun_fact: Its chambered shell has barely changed in 500 million years.
name: Chambered Nautilus

description: A pale cartilaginous fish from the chimaera order, sister to true sharks.
fun_fact: A chimaera, sister lineage to sharks since before there were trees.
name: Ghost Shark

description: A barrel-eyed fish with a transparent dome covering its tubular eyes.
fun_fact: Its skull is transparent so its tube eyes can swivel up through the dome.
name: Spookfish

description: A ribbon-thin deep-sea eel with extreme body elongation.
fun_fact: A ribbon-thin body that can hide three feet of length in slack water.
name: Snipe Eel

description: A blind hydrothermal-vent crab with hair-covered claws.
fun_fact: Found only at hydrothermal vents. The hairy claws farm bacteria they eat.
name: Yeti Crab

description: A jawless parasitic eel-shape that latches onto larger fish.
fun_fact: Has no jaw. Latches onto larger fish and rasps a wound until full.
name: Sea Lamprey

description: A primitive jawless fish that defends itself with massive amounts of slime.
fun_fact: Has no spine or jaw. Defends itself by producing buckets of slime in seconds.
name: Pacific Hagfish

description: An abyssal hunter that stands on three elongated fin rays above the seafloor.
fun_fact: Stands on three stilts on the abyssal floor and feels for prey in the current.
name: Tripod Fish

description: A walking sea cucumber that roams the abyssal plain in herds.
fun_fact: A sea cucumber that walks the abyss on tube-feet. Roams in herds.
name: Sea Pig

description: A rarely-seen deep-sea cephalopod with arms that trail far behind its body.
fun_fact: Found only at depth past three miles. Its arms are ten times its body.
name: Bigfin Squid

description: A pale deep-sea octopus that nests on warm hydrothermal vents.
fun_fact: Lays its eggs on hydrothermal vents. The young hatch from the heat.
name: Vent Octopus

description: A long, predatory deep-sea fish with light-producing barbels.
fun_fact: Lures prey with a glowing barbel. Its teeth are transparent so the lure isn't blocked.
name: Black Dragonfish
